title: Testing modules: validate, unit tests and an end-to-end run

videos.script: Ana wrote a module for the shop's network. It has two rules, and it works on her laptop. {{module}} Then a colleague renames the subnets, with a change that looks harmless. Nothing checks it. The first person to notice is somebody whose lookup stopped finding them. {{regression}} This lesson is about testing infrastructure code before anybody depends on it. Not one test, but a ladder of them, from free to real. {{ladder}} The cheapest rungs check the files: their layout, and whether they agree with the providers. They never look at a value. {{validate}} Then come tests written in HCL itself. A run plans the module with values you choose, and asserts what the plan would do. {{plan}} A mock provider lets the same tests run with no cloud at all. And a test can prove that a rule refuses the value it was written for. {{mocks}} At the bottom, one test builds the network for real, asks AWS what exists, and destroys it. It finds the mistake no plan can see. {{apply}} By the end, the module carries eight test runs, and half of them need no AWS at all. {{suite}}
